principles.name: Stage one hero object in a lit scene, not in a card
principles.description: The Opal home screen is built around a single object, the gem, placed in a full-bleed 3D environment. It has no container, border or card. The scene covers roughly the top 45% of the first screen and fades into black, and everything else on the page sits below it and supports it. For Maple, the tree (with its leaves) should be staged this way: a full-bleed night scene with sky gradient, ground/plinth and one soft light pool. It should not be a 72pt leaf inside a GlowCard.
principles.evidence: Seen in App Store screenshot 6 ('For better sleep, focus, and rest.') and in the opalapp.com render Frame 1171280249: the gem sits on a black puck on a rock plinth inside a canyon, lit by one shaft of light, with no surrounding UI chrome. Maple M0 (m0-today.png) puts the leaf at about 14% of screen width inside the first of three identical bordered cards.

principles.name: The hero sets the tint
principles.description: The colour of the current gem becomes the accent for the whole home screen: the score numeral, the trend glyph, the sub-score capsule strokes, the captions and the colour of the light shaft. Changing the gem is literally called 'Apply Theme'. For Maple, the current season or leaf species should tint the score and its breakdown (spring green, gold, crimson, frost). The amber #E8A35C stays reserved for newly earned rewards and the streak.
principles.evidence: Verified by comparing two official renders. With the blue-white opal, the score '85' and the capsules are icy blue and the light is cool. With the green-orange gem (opalapp.com 'Your day in one score'), the same UI is pale yellow-green and the light cone is warm. help.opalapp.com/article/how-to-choose-your-gem: long-press the gem, swipe, tap 'Apply Theme', and the gem changes on the Home tab and in the widget.

principles.name: One number, then three, then everything else
principles.description: The hierarchy is strict: one big score, a hairline bracket that branches into exactly three sub-scores (Sleep / Focus / Rest), and only then cards. The branching connector draws the composition of the score. For Maple these connectors can literally be drawn as branches from the trunk to the Sleep / Focus / Screen sub-scores.
principles.evidence: From the App Store screenshot at full resolution: 'Score' label, numeral '85' with a ▲, then 1px low-opacity bracket lines down to three capsules (moon 50, hourglass 86, tree 100) captioned Sleep, Focus, Rest. The opalapp.com copy describes the Opal Score as combining sleep, focus and rest signals into one measure.

principles.name: Explain the score; this is where Opal falls short
principles.description: Opal's users complain that the score breakdown page is never explained: what 'Ok' means, what 'Avg' is compared against, and why bars of different lengths can carry the same label. Maple's planned 'transparent breakdown' should beat Opal here. Each row should state its rule in plain words (e.g. 'Phone down before 23:00 — 0 min in bed = Great') and say what would improve it.
principles.evidence: community.opalapp.com thread 10906: the score page lists Phone in Bed, First hour phone use, Sitting, Sleep, First pickup, Last scroll and two Screen Time rows, with ratings and segmented or continuous bars. The poster asks for definitions and tooltips, and the reply confirms the UI does not explain any of it.

principles.name: Black does the work; light is local
principles.description: The background is close to pure black. Colour and glow come only from the hero (the gem's bloom and the light shaft) and from per-item colour blooms in the collection. Cards have no outer glow. They are separated from the background by a 1px top-lit gradient hairline and a very slight change in fill. For Maple, take the blue outer glow off every GlowCard and keep glow for leaves and the tree. Navy works better as the night-sky gradient behind the tree than as the fill of every card.
principles.evidence: Computed CSS on opalapp.com: body background rgb(4,4,4). Gem cards have a transparent fill and a ::before 1px border, linear-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,.10) to rgba(255,255,255,.02)), with no box-shadow. The colour comes from a glow image (blue-glow.webp, 625x625, opacity 0.7) clipped inside the card, plus a gem halo layer at opacity 0.5. Maple M0 GlowCard: navy fill, white-to-blue border and a blue shadow of radius 18 on every card.

principles.name: Few containers, each one live
principles.description: Opal's first home screen shows exactly one card under the hero (My Apps), and it holds live state (2 active rules, locked app icons). There are no explanatory paragraphs and no 'coming soon' cards. A feature appears only when it has state to show. Maple M0's three equal-weight cards (icon, title, paragraph, 'Arrives in M1' pill) are what make it read as templated or vibecoded.
principles.evidence: From Frame 1171280249 and App Store screenshot 6. Compare docs/screenshots/m0-today.png: three cards with the same template and the same border glow, describing features instead of showing data.

principles.name: Locked rewards look like raw material
principles.description: Locked milestones are shown as uncut grey rocks with a thin progress bar. They are not padlocks and not greyed-out copies of the gem. Revealing one cracks the rock open. For Maple, locked leaves could be bare twigs or buds, closed seeds, or a vein-only skeleton leaf that unfurls into colour when earned.
principles.evidence: screensdesign.com captures (3.x era): the Milestones grid of grey rocks named Invested (3 days), Steadfast (7 days), Radiant (30 days), Prismatic, Legendary, each with a mini progress bar. The First Gem reveal starts as a grey rock with a tap-to-reveal caption, followed by a shattering frame. opalapp.com/blog/the-milestone-reveal-moment: the concept comes from how opals are mined.

principles.name: The reveal is a ritual with physics, sound and haptics
principles.description: Earning a reward gets a dedicated full-screen black moment: a small header, the object in the centre, one caption-sized instruction, tap, a physical break-apart (debris flying off-screen), a reward sound and tuned haptics, then the name, the condition and one CTA. The home screen stays calm because all the drama goes here. This maps directly to Maple's morning leaf reveal.
principles.evidence: Opal blog 'the milestone reveal moment': 3D animations by a gem specialist animator, an iOS engineer tuning haptics, 'bits of dirt flying off the screen', reward sounds, and more than 2 million reveals. screensdesign captures: header 'Gem Unlocked / First Gem', rock, 'TAP TO REVEAL YOUR GEM', the gem with a teal bloom, then a pastel-gradient 'Save' button.

principles.name: Named, tiered and seasonal collectibles
principles.description: Each reward has a name and a plain unlock condition. Names escalate as adjectives by threshold (Driven at 10h, Determined at 50h, Diligent at 100h, Dutiful at 500h, Devoted at 1,000h focus). There are also calendar-limited ones (Spring, Summer Solstice, Winter Holidays, Earth Day, Holi, Ramadan, Easter, Passover, Valentine's) and social ones (Loyal, Soulful, Popular). Detail sheets show rarity. Maple's species and seasonal-colour catalogue fits this structure directly.
principles.evidence: The opalapp.com 'Focus Gems' section lists every gem with its unlock condition. The screensdesign First Gem detail sheet shows a small gold chip that appears to read 'Owned by 98%' (low-res capture, so partly inferred).

principles.name: Restrained navigation; status lives in the header
principles.description: Three tabs in a floating glass capsule. Profile and milestones are behind the avatar, and the streak is a small amber flame plus a number in the header, not a card. Maple's five tabs (Today, Sleep, Focus, Grove, Insights) are two too many for this style.
principles.evidence: Frame 1171280249 / 1171280248 tab bar: Home, My Apps, Timer. Header: amber flame '77' and a circular avatar. The older 3.x version had 4 tabs (Home, Blocks, Leaderboard, Profile; screensdesign). Oura made a similar cut from 5 tabs to 3 (Oura blog).

principles.name: Use physical metaphors for tools
principles.description: Opal's focus timer is a 3D-rendered object: a chunky device with a seven-segment LCD showing 30:00, set inside the same rock world. Below it sit a −/30m/+ stepper and a full-width Start capsule. Maple's bedtime or focus countdown could likewise be one crafted object (a moon dial, a lantern) instead of a text card.
principles.evidence: App Store screenshot 5 ('One tap. Total focus.') and the opalapp.com render Frame 1171280248 (Timer).

opal.home_screen_anatomy:
Opal 4.x home. Sources: App Store screenshot 6 at 1242x2688, and the opalapp.com render 'Frame 1171280249.png', which includes the tab bar. Vertical positions are measured from the renders as a percentage of screen height (393x852pt iPhone). They are approximate.

0. The status bar sits directly over the scene. There is no navigation-bar background.
1. Header row at ~10%. On the left is the custom 'Opal' wordmark, white at ~90%, about the visual size of a 28pt title, with a ~16pt margin. On the right are a streak indicator (small amber flame glyph plus '77' in amber, with no chip background) and a ~32pt circular avatar (an illustrated classical bust) with a thin light ring. There is no large title, no greeting and no settings gear.
2. Hero scene, full-bleed, from 0% to ~48%. A 3D render of a dark grey rocky canyon or cave. Rock walls frame the left and right edges, a starfield shows through the gap, and one soft volumetric light shaft from top centre falls on the gem. The gem's centre is at ~24% height. It is ~26–30% of screen width and ~16–19% of screen height, and it sits on a small black cylindrical puck on a flat rock plinth. The scene dissolves into black at the bottom with no hard edge. Visually this is ~45% of the first screen and the only saturated colour on it.
3. Score block at ~41–46%, overlapping the plinth. A small regular 'Score' label sits above a large semibold numeral '85' (about 3x the label size; its cap height is about a quarter of the gem's height), with a small solid ▲ trend glyph to the right. All of it is tinted with the gem's hue.
4. Breakdown at ~52–57%. A 1px low-opacity bracket branches from under the numeral to three capsules: [moon 50] [hourglass 86] [tree 100]. Each capsule's outline is a partial progress stroke in the gem tint (Sleep at 50 is about half lit, Rest at 100 is nearly fully lit). Small tinted semibold captions read Sleep / Focus / Rest.
5. One card starting at ~62%. Full width minus ~16pt margins, ~24–28pt radius, a charcoal fill only slightly lighter than the background, and a faint top highlight. Inside: a header 'My Apps >' (secondary grey with a chevron, sentence case), a row with a shield glyph and '2 active rules', a hairline divider, then a row of app icons in rounded squares with lock glyphs labelled 'Unblock'.
6. A floating glass pill 'Manage Apps' (grid icon) overlaps the bottom of that card.
7. A floating glass capsule tab bar at ~91%: Home (ring icon), My Apps (2x2 grid), Timer (play triangle), each with a tiny label.

Below the fold (from release notes, not seen directly): a Screen Time card with today's total and most-used apps (v4.3.1), and insight cards (v4.10). The insight card style appears in App Store screenshot 4. It is a frosted glass card with an 'Insights >' header, a centred bed line-icon, a two-line bold sentence giving the user's typical phone-down time with the time range in the accent tint, a 'Most Used Before Bed' list of three apps showing average minutes, and a glass capsule CTA 'Learn Bedtime Tips'.

Older 2023 home (Opal blog): today's screen time, Focus Score %, and pickups at the top; then a scrubbable hourly bar chart in green (focus) and red (distracted); then a per-app list. The gem was decorative, and its colour stood for positive focus time.

Weight ranking on the 4.x first screen: hero scene >> score numeral > three capsules > card > tab bar. Everything below the hero is greyscale except the borrowed tint.
opal.hero_visual:
Lighting recipe, consistent across the app, the website and the detail sheets (observed):
- The background is black or near-black.
- One key light from above: a visible volumetric cone on the home screen.
- A soft radial bloom directly behind the object, in the object's own hue. On the web this is a separate glow PNG at 50–70% opacity.
- The object always sits on the same small black cylindrical pedestal or puck (opalapp.com uses a dedicated 'gem-stand.png' under every gem).
- The object has bright rim and specular highlights, so it reads as physical and glassy.
- The environment (rock walls) darkens the frame edges like a vignette.

On Home, the gem is ~26–30% of screen width, horizontally centred, with its centre at ~24% of screen height, inside a full-bleed scene that takes up the top ~45% and fades to black. No card or border surrounds it. The gem's hue changes the score and capsule tint and the colour of the light cone: cool icy light for the blue-white opal, warm yellow light for the green-orange gem.

Gem detail sheet (3.x capture): the gem is ~45% of width, centred on the puck, with a large teal bloom behind it on black.

Reveal screen: the object is centred at ~45–50% width on pure black, with no environment.

Motion of the hero: the Opal blog says Apple's Screen Time privacy rules forced the home gem into a sandboxed extension that allowed no animation. The home gem was therefore essentially a still render, and its premium feel comes from render quality and lighting, not movement. (It is not confirmed whether 4.x has since added motion.) The stated design intent was for the gem to keep 'growing brighter, more vibrant, and more intricate as your focus improves', so the hero evolves with progress.

Users choose which gem is the hero by long-pressing it, swiping, and tapping 'Apply Theme'. The choice also applies to the widget.

Maple translation (recommendation): full-bleed night sky (#05070D at the top to #0B1426), a low ground hill or plinth, the procedural Canvas tree centred, one soft moonlight pool from above, and a low-opacity bloom behind the canopy in the dominant leaf colour. No GlowCard around it. The tree should take ~40–45% of the first screen.
opal.typography:
Verified from opalapp.com computed CSS: the font is the system stack (system-ui / -apple-system, i.e. SF Pro).
- Hero H1: 81.6px, weight 700, letter-spacing −0.82px (−1%), line-height 1.1.
- Section headings: 51.9px, weight 600, line-height 1.2.
- Body: 18.5px, weight 400, white at 80% opacity, line-height ~1.6–1.7.
- Gem labels: 14.8px, weight 400, white at 80%, centred.
- Eyebrows ('Focus Gems ®', 'Opal Score ®'): small regular text inside a dark pill with a hairline border, not tracked caps.

In-app (observed from renders; sizes are estimates):
- Wordmark: custom.
- Score numeral: SF Pro semibold. It is the default SF Pro, not Rounded (flat-topped 5) and not monospaced, at roughly 44–56pt, with a solid ▲ trend glyph next to it.
- 'Score' label: ~15pt regular.
- Capsule values: ~15–17pt semibold with an inline SF Symbol.
- Captions under capsules: ~12pt semibold, tinted.
- Card headers: ~15–17pt medium, secondary grey, sentence case with a chevron ('My Apps >', 'Insights >', 'Rules >'), placed inside the card.
- Nav titles: centred ~17pt semibold ('Rules'). Page titles: left-aligned ~28pt semibold ('Timer', 'Apps').

Number styling:
- Durations are written '1h 23m' with a space and units at the same size and weight.
- Comparisons read like '4h 04m a day', with the better value in the accent tint.
- Under a ring numeral there is a small tracked uppercase qualifier ('LESS THAN USUAL').
- The website counter of hours saved uses rolling odometer digits.

Reward moments only (3.x captures): a condensed bold uppercase display face for 'DAY STREAK', 'FOCUS HOURS', 'FIRST GEM' and the huge streak numeral, set in gold or teal, plus tiny tracked caps CTAs ('TAP TO REVEAL YOUR GEM').

The timer uses skeuomorphic seven-segment LCD digits.

Home uses sentence case throughout, with no tracked-caps section eyebrows. Maple M0's 'YOUR MAPLE' eyebrow and its large-title 'Rest well' are both absent from Opal's home pattern.
opal.color_and_light:
Background: opalapp.com body is rgb(4,4,4) (verified). App screens are black or near-black, and the rock environment is desaturated charcoal grey.

Colour sources are strictly limited (observed):
1. The hero gem, its bloom and the light shaft.
2. The same hue borrowed as a tint for the score numeral, the trend glyph, the capsule strokes and captions, and highlighted values in insight text. This is icy blue-white (~#CFE6F5, estimated) for the opal and pale yellow-green for the green gem.
3. Amber or gold only for the streak (flame glyph plus count in the header; flame, numeral and 'DAY STREAK' on the streak screen, where a warm amber radial bloom fills the top third on black).
4. Green and red only in data bars (2023 chart; score-page bars).
5. Soft pastel gradients only on primary CTAs: lavender 'Start'; yellow-green to cyan 'Save'. These have dark text.

Glow technique on the web (verified CSS): glow is an image (blue-glow.webp, ice-glow.webp, yellow-glow.webp). It is placed at about 2.5x the card size (625px glow behind a 250px card), at opacity 0.7, offset negatively and clipped by overflow:hidden. A gem-specific halo image sits at opacity 0.5 behind each gem. There are no box-shadow glows on cards.

Marketing backgrounds (App Store) use a pale icy-blue gradient with floating rock fragments. This is brand framing, not in-app.

Relevance to Maple: Opal's sparing amber for the streak matches Maple's #E8A35C reward role almost exactly. The main difference from Maple M0 is that Opal never puts coloured glow on generic containers.
opal.surfaces_and_cards:
Web gem card (verified CSS):
- 250x313px (4:5 aspect), border-radius 42px (~17% of width).
- Transparent fill on #040404, with a 1px gradient hairline border via a masked ::before: rgba(255,255,255,0.10) at the top to rgba(255,255,255,0.02) at the bottom. The border is lit from above and fades out downward.
- Padding 16/32/32, overflow hidden, an internal colour glow image at 70% opacity.
- Gem image 186x232 with its halo at 50% opacity, pedestal image 186x56, label 15px at 80% white.
- Hover: scale transform over 0.3s.
- Cards sit 48px apart in a marquee.

In-app (observed):
- First screen of Home: exactly 1 card below the hero.
- Card fill is charcoal, barely lighter than the background (~#141416–#1C1C1E, estimated), with a faint top-edge highlight, radius ~24–28pt and ~16pt side margins. No visible drop shadow or outer glow.
- Rules screen: a 2-column grid of square-ish cards (~24pt radius). Each has a soft radial spotlight at the top (icy white fading to black) that gives a top-lit, slightly 3D feel. Top-left icon flow (calendar → shield), a status chip ('7 left', 'in 12h', or '⚠ Issue Detected' in yellow), a semibold title ('10PM—8AM'), and a sublabel with tiny app icons. Inactive or paused cards drop to ~40% opacity.
- Insights card: frosted translucent glass with background blur, hairline light border and centred content.
- Elevation comes from translucency and top light, never from shadows.

Cards per screen: Home 1 (plus the hero); Rules 4–5 small tiles; Timer 0 cards (one hero object plus controls), then a horizontal 'For You' carousel of photo cards.
opal.buttons_and_controls:
Observed in renders and captures:

Primary buttons:
- Full-width capsules, ~50pt tall, with a soft pastel gradient fill: lavender-to-grey 'Start' with a ▶ glyph on Timer; yellow-green to cyan 'Save' with dark text on the gem-unlocked screen.
- 'Current Gem' on the gem detail sheet is a full-width dark grey capsule with a ✓.

Secondary buttons:
- Glass capsules: translucent, blurred, with a thin light border ('Learn Bedtime Tips', the floating 'Manage Apps' pill with a grid icon).
- Outlined capsules in the reward colour on milestone screens ('My Progress →' in a gold outline).

Steppers: a −/+ pair of ~44pt glass circles flanking a wide glass capsule showing the value ('30m', ~22pt medium).

Toggle-as-chip: a small capsule 'Block Apps No' with a shield glyph, the label in white and the value in dimmer grey.

Status chips: small dark capsules ('7 left', 'in 12h'), plus a warning chip with yellow text.

Header buttons: ~36pt circular glass back button (chevron) top-left; ~36pt circular '+' with an icy-blue gradient fill top-right.

Score sub-score capsules: outline capsules (~2:1 aspect) whose stroke doubles as a progress meter in the tint colour. They read as both button and gauge.

Unblock tiles: app icons inside rounded squares with a lock glyph and a small 'Unblock' label, in a glass tray.

No filled-colour rectangular buttons and no heavy shadows anywhere.
opal.navigation:
Opal 4.x (observed in the opalapp.com renders): 3 top-level tabs in a floating, inset glass capsule tab bar about 60% of screen width, centred above the home indicator: Home (ring/opal icon), My Apps (2x2 grid), Timer (play triangle), each with a tiny label.
- Profile, MileStones and stats are reached from the avatar at top right.
- The streak is a header glyph that leads to the streak screen.
- Rules is reached from a 'Rules >' header link and a centred-title push screen with a circular back button and a '+' button.
- Milestones and gem detail open as sheets (a grabber is visible in the captures).

Opal 3.x (screensdesign captures): 4 tabs (Home, Blocks, Leaderboard, Profile) plus a persistent mini session sheet docked above the tab bar ('Session 00:57:05 · My Event', with a chevron), similar to Apple Music's mini player.

The release notes for 4.0 describe renaming Blocks to Rules and Breaks to Unblock, and adding Timer, Opal Score and Autofocus. The structure was consolidated.

Comparable: Oura cut 5 tabs (Home, Readiness, Sleep, Activity, Resilience) to 3 (Today, Vitals, My Health).

Implication for Maple (recommendation): collapse the 5 tabs to 3, e.g. Home (tree + tonight/morning state), a Rest/Focus tools tab, and Herbarium. Put Insights under Home cards or the profile, and put the streak and leaf count in the header.
opal.motion:
Verified:
- On opalapp.com the gem collection is a slow horizontal marquee with a 60s loop (class 'c-marquee cc-60s'; transform observed advancing between screenshots).
- Cards scale on hover over 0.3s.
- Sections fade up on scroll ('cc-fade-up').
- The hours-saved counter rolls odometer-style. Digits were caught mid-roll in two screenshots.

Verified (Opal blog, milestone reveal):
- The reveal is a 3D animation by a specialist gem animator: tap the rock, it breaks open with debris flying off the screen, and reward sounds plus hand-tuned haptics play.
- The home gem lives in a sandboxed Screen Time extension that allowed no animation, so the home hero was static.

Observed in still captures (motion inferred):
- The 'Driven Gem' achievement shows the earned gem large in the centre, with other gems and sparkle particles floating around it in black space. This implies a slow drift or orbit.
- The streak screen has a glowing flame with a large warm bloom (probably a flicker).

Inferred overall pattern: the persistent screens are almost motionless, and every bit of animation, sound and haptics is spent on reward and reveal moments. This fits Maple's 'sleepy, not hyper' brief.

Maple suggestion: a very slow canopy sway or breathing (6–10s cycles), the occasional single leaf drift, and a one-time unfurl or reveal ritual with a soft haptic on the morning check-in. Everything should become static under Reduce Motion, as Opal's home already effectively is.
opal.reward_collection_ui:
Milestones sheet (3.x captures, low-res):
- 'MileStones' title left; top right shows a percentage collected with a thin progress bar.
- Sections by category. Each section has a hero: a glowing glyph (gold flame for DAY STREAK, teal-green hourglass for FOCUS HOURS), a condensed uppercase coloured title, a one-line grey explanation, and an outlined capsule 'My Progress →'.
- Under each section, a 3-column grid of milestones. Locked items are uncut grey rocks with a thin progress bar beneath, then the name and requirement: Invested (3 days), Steadfast (7 days), Radiant (30 days), Prismatic, Legendary.

Profile (3.x):
- Hexagon avatar plus a generated 'gem name' username.
- A horizontal row of owned gem thumbnails (coloured) followed by locked ones (grey rocks).
- Two side-by-side cards (Day Streak, Focus Hours), each with its glowing glyph and a 'next milestone' progress row.

Gem detail sheet:
- Uppercase condensed name ('FIRST GEM'), the condition below it ('You Installed Opal'), and a small gold rarity chip (appears to read 'Owned by 98%').
- The gem large on its pedestal with a colour-matched bloom, an unlock date row, a one-line description, a full-width '✓ Current Gem' button (sets it as the home theme), and a share icon at top right. Share produces an image card; the photo picker capture shows the First Gem card saved as an image.

Reveal flow:
- Black screen with header 'Gem Unlocked' / name.
- A grey rock in the centre with the tiny caption 'TAP TO REVEAL YOUR GEM'.
- The rock shatters to reveal the iridescent gem with its bloom.
- Then a congratulations line and a pastel 'Save' CTA.

Streak screen: a huge glowing flame, a large gold numeral, 'DAY STREAK', one explanatory sentence, a 7-day row in a hairline-bordered card (completed days are filled gold circles with ✓), and a dim gold footer with a bit of lore (the etymology of 'focus' as hearth).

Website 'Hall of gems': two rows of 4:5 cards in a 60s marquee.

Catalogue structure (opalapp.com):
- Progression gems named as escalating adjectives: Driven 10h, Determined 50h, Diligent 100h, Dutiful 500h, Devoted 1,000h focus.
- Usage gems: Motivated 2 days, Committed 5 days, Balanced 10 days.
- Social gems: Loyal 1 friend, Soulful 3, Popular 10.
- Status gems: Original (early adopter), Unwavering (Pro), First (install).
- Calendar-limited gems: Spring (first day of spring), Summer (solstice), Winter (holidays), Earth Day, Easter, Holi, Ramadan, Passover, Love (Valentine's).

This maps one-to-one onto Maple's species and seasonal colours, with the rare frosted winter leaf as a limited-time item.
what_makes_it_feel_premium_not_generic: The hero is a crafted, physically lit 3D object in an environment (cave, light shaft, pedestal), not an SF Symbol or flat vector inside a card. Maple's procedural tree needs comparable craft: real branching, leaf variation, light falloff and ground contact shadow.
One focal point per screen. Home has a gem; Timer has an LCD clock object; the reveal has a rock. Nothing competes for attention.
Colour comes from content (the gem), and the rest of the UI borrows it. Chrome is greyscale, so the reward always looks precious.
No glow on containers. Cards use a 1px top-lit hairline (10% to 2% white) and nearly the same fill as the background, so they recede and the hero glows.

Consistent presentation grammar: every gem sits on the same black puck with the same bloom recipe on the website, the home screen and the detail sheet. That repetition reads as a system, not one-off decoration.
A data hierarchy that reads in one second: big number, three sub-numbers joined by hairline branches, then cards. No paragraphs on Home.

Copy is short, human and a little witty. The block screen says you set this rule yesterday and past you was right. There's a Focus Haiku option and etymology lore on the streak screen, and users are called 'gems'. There is no dev-speak (contrast Maple's 'Arrives in M1').
Rewards are rituals: tap to reveal, physical debris, sound, tuned haptics, a name and a rarity figure. This makes a collectible feel earned, not dispensed.
Locked items are shown as raw material (uncut rock), which creates anticipation instead of the 'greyed-out list' feel.
Controls are glass capsules and circles with hairline borders, and primary CTAs use soft pastel gradients. There are no saturated filled rectangles and no heavy shadows.
Navigation is restrained: 3 floating tabs, with the streak and profile in the header. Fewer, deeper screens instead of many shallow tabs of placeholder cards.
Marketing-grade renders are used in the product itself (the same cave world on the website hero and in the app), so the brand world is continuous.

other_reference_apps.lesson: Make Home a time-aware front page, not a fixed stack. Oura cut 5 tabs to 3 (Today, Vitals, My Health). Today is modelled on a news app's top stories: score shortcuts at the top, then one daily highlight that changes with the time of day you open the app, then a timeline. For Maple: evenings lead with the wind-down/bedtime countdown, mornings lead with last night's leaf reveal, and the tree stays the constant hero. (Verified from Oura's 'new Oura app experience' blog. Oura's scenic time-of-day header imagery is from prior knowledge, not re-verified.)

Lead with one plain headline number that changes behaviour (sleep debt in hours over the last 14 nights), with a derived 0–100 score secondary to it. Rise is explicit about its window and keeps a deliberate 14-night scope. For Maple: one tonight number (time until wind-down) and a transparent wellbeing score whose window and rules are stated on screen. (Verified from Rise help centre and blog; visual style not verified.)

A monochrome UI where the only expressive visual is a generative graphic tied to the current state: thin white lines and sparkling dots on black, with organic, never jarring motion. For Maple: render the night sky and tree procedurally in Canvas with fine linework and slow drift, let the app's state (season, streak, time of night) drive the visuals, and keep everything else monochrome. (Verified from the Readymag feature and screensdesign review.)

Proof that a growing-tree loop and a large species catalogue (90 to 100+ tree species unlocked by milestones, reviewed as a forest map by week, month or year) sustain long-term engagement. Its punitive mechanic, where the tree withers if you leave the app, is exactly what Maple rejects. Borrow the catalogue and the week/month/year herbarium views, and keep Maple's rule that bad nights only make the tree quieter and never remove leaves. critique.overall_verdict: The user is right. M0 reads as stock AI-generated SwiftUI: one generic component (an SF Symbol, a bold title, two grey lines and a pill, inside a bordered navy card with a glow) is copied onto every tab. The product's one idea, the maple tree, is missing from the home screen. The only maple on screen is a 56pt Canadian-flag polygon tucked into the corner of a card. Nothing on the home screen is real data. There are no numbers, no tree, no collection and no motion, just a roadmap with "Arrives in M1" stickers. The glow border, which should signal "special", sits on every surface, so it reads as a template effect. It also leaves grey halos between the stacked cards. Opal is the opposite: one luminous hero object on near-black (its gem), one or two big numbers, a bright primary action, and very little chrome. The fix is structural, not cosmetic. (1) Replace the Today card stack with a custom header plus a full-bleed tree "stage" that takes about 55–60% of the first screen, then one big-number stat row, then one or two compact contextual rows. (2) Replace the flag polygon with a family of drawn, botanical leaf species. (3) Use glow and borders only on the hero, the reward moments and the primary CTA. (4) Cut the tab bar to 3–4 tabs, with sleep and focus started from Home. (5) Remove all milestone placeholders from the UI. The palette, token architecture, motion tokens, accessibility work and calm copy voice are good foundations and should stay. Note: the leaf catalog the user mentioned isn't in the repo yet (I searched the project for catalog, leaf and image files), so the species list below is a starting proposal to reconcile with it.

issues.problem: There is no maple on display. The 'hero' is a horizontal HStack with a 56pt LeafGlyph on the left and an overline, headline and body text on the right, inside the same GlowCard as everything else. It covers about 15% of the screen and has the same visual weight as the two placeholder cards below it. The user explicitly asked for 'a home page with the maple on display'.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: It's the default 'list of cards' home that AI scaffolds produce. Nothing is the obvious focal point, and the brand object is shown as a thumbnail icon instead of a living thing. Opal's home is built around one large rendered object; this one is built around a VStack.
issues.fix: Build a TreeStage view: an unboxed, full-width Canvas tree with no card, border or fill, sitting straight on the background and using about 55–60% of the first viewport height. Add a soft radial light behind it, tinted by season and time of night. Overlay or place directly under it the leaf count as a large StatNumber (e.g. '12 leaves'), with streak and season as one quiet secondary line. Empty state: draw a bare sapling with a single bud, not an earned amber leaf. Keep the line 'Keep tonight's bedtime and you'll find it here in the morning' as the caption under the sapling. Tapping the tree opens the Grove/Herbarium.

issues.area: PlaceholderCard template, every tab (Shared/PlaceholderCard.swift, Sleep/Focus/Grove/Insights views)
issues.problem: Every screen is a stack of the same component: grey SF Symbol (title2) at top-left, a semibold headline, 2–3 lines of grey callout, an 'Arrives in Mx' capsule. Five tabs, eleven cards, one layout. No screen has a shape of its own.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: Icon, title and description in a rounded card is the classic AI 'feature card'. It's a landing-page feature grid presented as an app. When every tab has the same layout, nobody designed the individual screens.
issues.fix: Delete PlaceholderCard from shipping UI. Build each screen around its real content. Sleep: a large bedtime clock or arc with wind-down and wake times as big numbers. Focus: one large timer dial with a start pill. Grove: tree plus herbarium grid. Insights: one chart with a transparent score breakdown. For features that aren't built yet, either hide the entry or show a real but dormant control (e.g. a disabled 'Sounds' row) without explaining the roadmap.

issues.problem: 'Arrives in M1', 'Arrives in M2' and 'Export and delete arrive in M7' (Settings) expose internal milestone codes. The body copy describes features instead of being them, e.g. 'A countdown to wind-down and bedtime, based on the schedule you set up in onboarding.' It even mentions 'onboarding', which users never think about.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: Shipping dev-plan vocabulary and explanatory blurbs is the clearest sign that a model generated the UI from a spec document. Premium apps show state ('Wind-down in 1h 20m'), not descriptions of state.
issues.fix: Remove every milestone string from the UI and keep the roadmap in docs/. Write state-first, short copy: 'Wind-down 22:30 · Bed 23:00', 'Last night: 7h 12m', 'No leaf yet — tonight's the night.' Each line should be 6 words or fewer where possible, with the number carrying the meaning.

issues.problem: The leaf is a 27-point straight-line polygon of the Canadian flag silhouette, with a rectangular spike for a stem, no veins, no curvature and no serration variety. It's filled with an opacity-only diagonal gradient (0.95 to 0.7) plus a 18% white stroke and a coloured shadow. All four 'seasons' are the same silhouette recoloured, and spring #9CBF86 and summer #6E9A6B are hard to tell apart at this size.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: It reads as the 🍁 emoji or a flag, not a botanical object, and polygon-to-Path code is an obvious AI shortcut. It also makes the user's main ask ('lot of other types of maple leaves') impossible, because you can't build a collection from one silhouette with a hue swap.
issues.fix: Build a LeafSpecies model where each species has its own drawn outline using quadratic/cubic curves, a petiole that tapers and curves, primary veins drawn as separate strokes at about 25–35% opacity, and a fine serration pass on the edge. Candidate species: Sugar (5-lobed, rounded sinuses), Red (3-lobed, serrated), Silver (deeply cut), Japanese palmate (7–9 slender lobes), Japanese laceleaf (dissected), Norway (broad, pointed), Field (small, blunt lobes), Bigleaf (huge), Vine (round, 7–9 shallow lobes), Amur (3-lobed, elongated centre), Paperbark (trifoliate), Striped/Moosewood (goose-foot). Then layer colourways on top: spring green, summer green, gold, crimson, frosted, plus a rare variegated or two-tone. Shading: a radial light from the top-left plus a slightly darker midrib side, with no outer shadow at small sizes. Each leaf should look like a pressed specimen, which also suits the herbarium.

issues.area: Border and glow treatment (GlowCard / glowSurface / MapleButtonStyle)
issues.problem: Every surface gets the same treatment: a 1pt white (22%) to blue (10%) gradient stroke, plus a blue shadow (radius 18, 16% opacity). That covers cards, primary buttons and the leaves showcase. In the screenshot, stacked cards' halos merge into muddy grey bands in the 24pt gaps, and the white top-edge highlight repeats down the page like a ladder.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: A gradient-border glow card on dark navy is the 'dark glassmorphism dashboard' cliché that AI tools produce by default. Applied everywhere, it stops meaning 'special' and becomes texture.
issues.fix: Use three levels of surface. Level 0: content sits directly on the background, with no card. Level 1: quiet tiles with a fill of about #0E182C (or white at 4%), no border and no shadow, used for secondary rows. Level 2: the spec's thin white/soft-blue border plus a very faint glow, used ONLY for the primary CTA, the morning leaf-reveal card and the share card. Drop the glow radius to about 24 at about 8–10% so it reads as ambient light, not a drop shadow. Never stack two Level-2 elements next to each other.

issues.problem: There are five tabs (Today, Sleep, Focus, Grove, Insights) with stock SF Symbols: sun.horizon, moon.stars, timer, a generic leaf (not a maple) and chart.bar.xaxis. Three of the five tabs hold only 2–3 placeholder cards. The tint is textPrimary, so selected and unselected icons are both white, and selection is shown only by a darker recessed capsule on a light glass bar. The tab bar is the brightest large surface on screen.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: One tab per feature is the scaffold default ('make a tab for each section of the spec'). The stock filled symbols in mismatched styles (sun, moon with sparkles, stopwatch, leaf, bar chart) look like a starter template. A generic leaf for a maple app is a brand miss.
issues.fix: Go to 3–4 tabs, e.g. Home (tree), Grove (herbarium and collection), Insights, and optionally Sessions. Sleep wind-down, focus start and sounds become primary actions launched from Home as sheets or full-screen modes, which is how Opal starts a session. Use a custom maple-leaf tab icon for Grove. Show the unselected state at textSecondary and the selected state at textPrimary. Keep the system Liquid Glass bar but darken its tint so it sits below the hero visually.

issues.problem: FeatureScreen uses .navigationTitle, so every screen opens with a 34pt system large title ('Rest well', 'Sleep', 'Focus') and a lone Liquid Glass gear button on its own row above it. Together they use about 180pt of the most valuable space before any content. The title is SF Pro Bold, which ignores the tokens' claim that headings are SF Rounded.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: This is the stock iOS Settings/Health look. A time-of-day greeting as the page title ('Good morning') is a common AI home-screen pattern, and it carries no information.
issues.fix: Hide the nav bar on Home and draw a compact custom header: a small rounded date or context line ('Fri · Bedtime in 1h 20m') on the left and a small avatar/settings button on the right, about 44pt tall in total. Hand the space it frees to the tree. Use inline titles or no titles on the other tabs, and keep large titles only for list-like screens such as Settings. If a greeting stays, make it a small secondary line, not the H1.

issues.problem: The screen has three tiers: a large nav title, then 17pt headlines, then grey callout, repeated identically in each card. There is no large number anywhere, even though the spec says 'large readable numbers' and StatNumber exists. MapleFont.display is just .largeTitle (34pt), so the system has no true display or hero numeral size. The design-system type ramp is the five default text styles.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: A flat, repeated hierarchy with grey paragraphs is how generated UIs look when nobody decided what the user should read first. Opal leads with one big number, then a label, then very little else.
issues.fix: Add hero tokens: a 64–80pt SF Rounded numeral for the single key metric, scaled with @ScaledMetric, and a 28–34pt secondary numeral for stat rows, both monospacedDigit. Give Home exactly one hero number (leaf count or bedtime countdown) and at most three secondary numbers. Cut body paragraphs to one line. Make all headings SF Rounded consistently, including custom headers.

issues.problem: Everything uses the same rhythm: 24pt card padding, 24pt gaps, 20pt margins. Each placeholder card is about 240pt tall for two lines of text, so the first screen shows three boxes and very little information. Generosity without grouping looks empty, not calm.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: Uniform VStack spacing is the default output when no layout grid or grouping has been designed. Real calm comes from a big quiet hero plus tight, well-grouped secondary rows, not from evenly padded boxes.
issues.fix: Use deliberate contrast. A large hero gets 40–56pt of breathing room above and below. Secondary content is grouped in compact rows: a 56–64pt row height, 12pt between rows, 32pt between groups. Use a 24pt screen margin for the hero area if it helps the tree breathe, and keep 20pt for lists.

issues.problem: The primary button is a navy (#18264A) fill with the same glow border as the cards and white text. Secondary is a border at 10% opacity. In a screen full of glow cards, the primary action is indistinguishable from a card. Nothing says 'tap here'.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: When the button and the container share one treatment, the button reads as a template component, not a designed call to action. Opal's key actions are bright, solid pills that clearly sit above the dark UI.
issues.fix: Make the primary CTA a solid textPrimary (#F2F5FA) capsule with a near-black #05070D label, 56pt tall, SF Rounded semibold, plus the one allowed soft glow. Or keep the bordered navy pill for secondary use only. Use at most one primary CTA per screen, e.g. 'Start wind-down' in the evening and 'See last night's leaf' in the morning. Amber stays off buttons, per the spec.

issues.problem: The background is a flat linear #05070D to #0B1426 gradient, and cards are #111D35 on top, so the whole screen is one navy hue with lighter boxes and no light source or depth. The autumnGold leaf (#E8A35C) is the same hex as the reward accent, so in October the 'season' leaf and the 'reward' colour are identical and amber stops meaning reward. Crimson exists as a token but is unused. Frost #C9DCE8 next to white text looks like a disabled white icon.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: Navy-on-navy boxes with no ambient light are the default dark-theme look. Premium dark apps like Opal use true near-black with a coloured light bloom behind the hero, so the content glows rather than the containers.
issues.fix: Keep #05070D as the base and add a large, very soft radial bloom behind the tree, tinted by season (gold, green or frost at 10–15%) and dimmer late at night. Push card fills closer to the background (about #0C1527) so the hero is the brightest thing on screen. Separate the leaf palette from the reward token: give autumn gold a slightly different hue (e.g. #D99A4E) and reserve #E8A35C for reward UI. Spread spring and summer further apart (one yellow-green, one deep blue-green). Give frost a faint blue edge and an inner highlight so it reads as ice, not as white.

issues.problem: Each placeholder card opens with a grey SF Symbol (moon.zzz, sunrise, bed.double, waveform, hand.raised, timer, tree, book.closed and so on) that adds no information. The Settings privacy rows use lock.shield and square.and.arrow.up.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: An SF Symbol above every heading is a hallmark of generated UI: the icon just restates the title.
issues.fix: Remove icons that only restate the title. Where an icon is needed, use a small custom set that matches the leaf illustration style (thin rounded stroke, consistent weight), or replace the icon with real visual data such as a mini bedtime arc, a sound waveform or a timer ring.

issues.problem: Six swatches in a grid; 'Background' and 'Raised' are visually indistinguishable and have no hex values or usage notes. The leaves are shown as four recoloured copies of one polygon. The type ramp is just the names 'Display / Title / Headline' set in themselves. The components section has one card type and one button. The whole thing is bordered GlowCards again.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: This is the default 'design system page' a model generates. It shows the system is thin: one surface, one button, no hero, no leaf variety, no elevation levels.
issues.fix: Turn it into a working reference that matches the redesign. Show each swatch with its hex and its role ('reward only'). Show the three surface levels side by side. Add a leaf catalog grid of every species in every colourway, with the rare ones flagged. Add a numeral scale (hero, secondary, inline). Show the tree in 3–4 growth stages and in each season. Show the primary and secondary CTAs on real backgrounds. Lay it out with section dividers instead of boxing every section.

issues.problem: Nothing on Home moves. Motion.drift exists for 'the tree's sway' but there's no tree and no ambient motion. The glow is static, so the screen feels like a mockup.
issues.why_it_reads_generic_or_vibecoded: Static card stacks feel like a template screenshot. Opal's hero object breathes, which signals craft.
issues.fix: Give the tree stage a slow sway (3–6s cycles, a few degrees) and occasional drifting particles (falling leaf in autumn, snow in winter). Animate the bloom with a slow breathing glow. Make the morning leaf reveal a slow fade with a drift-down. Route everything through mapleAnimation and show a still frame under Reduce Motion. Use TimelineView with a low frame budget for the Canvas.

The calm, non-judgmental copy voice: 'Waiting for its first leaf', 'Keep tonight's bedtime and you'll find it here in the morning', 'Bad nights never take leaves away', 'Never leaves your iPhone'.
The seasonal leaf palette concept (spring, summer, gold, crimson, frost) and the real-season Season(for:hemisphere:) logic. Tune the hues and add species shapes on top.
